```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(varm)
set.seed(7)
y <- as.matrix(yraw)
colnames(y) <- c("inflation", "unemployment", "rate")
```

`bvarm()` fits a conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart BVAR with the prior of
Giannone, Lenza and Primiceri (2015), specified by `prior_minnesota()`:

- Minnesota shrinkage with overall tightness `lambda` and lag decay `alpha`;
- sum-of-coefficients (`soc`) and single-unit-root (`sur`) dummy-observation
  priors, each of which can be dropped by passing `NULL`;
- the inverse-Wishart scale `psi` (AR(p) residual variances by default);
- prior mean of the own first lag `delta` (1 for levels, 0 for growth rates).

Every hyperparameter is `c(mode, sd, min, max)` of a gamma hyperprior. The
character vector `hyper` selects which are estimated; the rest stay fixed.

## Fixed hyperparameters: exact posterior draws

With `hyper = character(0)` the posterior is sampled exactly (no MCMC, so
`nburn` is unused).

```{r fixed}
pr <- prior_minnesota(lambda = 0.2, soc = NULL, sur = NULL, hyper = character(0))
fit0 <- bvarm(y, p = 2, prior = pr, ndraw = 1000)
fit0
```

## Hierarchical hyperparameters

By default `lambda`, `soc` and `sur` are estimated: the mode is found by
`optim()` and a compiled Metropolis sampler with adaptive scale draws the
hyperparameters; coefficients and covariances are then drawn directly.

```{r hier}
fit <- bvarm(y, p = 2, ndraw = 1000, nburn = 500)
fit
colMeans(fit$hyper)
fit$accept       # Metropolis acceptance rate
fit$logml        # log marginal likelihood at the hyperparameter mode
```

Use `hyper = "full"` to also estimate `alpha` and `psi`. The marginal
likelihood can be used to compare prior settings or lag lengths.

```{r ml}
c(p1 = bvarm(y, p = 1, ndraw = 200, nburn = 200)$logml,
  p2 = fit$logml)
```

## Posterior summaries, IRFs and forecasts

`summary()` gives posterior means, standard deviations and 5/95% quantiles of
`B`. The `draws` element is a `varm_draws` object, the same container used by
the bootstrap, so all identification schemes work.

```{r post}
s <- summary(fit)
round(s$mean[1:3, ], 3)
max(stability(fit))   # largest eigenvalue modulus across draws
```

```{r irf}
ir <- irf(fit, id = id_chol(), horizon = 16)
ir
```

```{r irf-plot, fig.height = 4}
plot(ir, shocks = "rate")
```

Sign restrictions apply to Bayesian draws as well.

```{r sign}
S <- matrix(0, 3, 3, dimnames = list(colnames(y), c("mp", "s2", "s3")))
S["rate", "mp"] <- 1; S["inflation", "mp"] <- -1
irs <- irf(fit, id = id_sign(S, horizon = 2, maxtry = 2000), horizon = 12)
irs$accept_rate
```

```{r fc}
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 8)
round(fc$mean, 2)
```

`fevd()` and `hd()` (median over `ndraw` posterior draws) are available as
well.

## Not yet implemented

Stochastic-volatility, stochastic-search variable selection and other
shrinkage priors, time-varying-parameter VARs, non-conjugate and
independent Normal-Wishart priors, Gibbs samplers other than the
Minnesota/GLP one, and factor-augmented VARs. Although the package
`DESCRIPTION` mentions them, there is no code behind them yet.
